newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Trencor worried about trading conditions.
newsitem.headline: Trencor worried about trading conditions.

text.p: Soft trading conditions at home and abroad and uncertainty about the rand exchange rate made it difficult to forecast earnings, container company Trencor Ltd chairman Neil Jowell said on Friday.
"The soft market conditions and certain adverse shipping industry trends continue to be cause for concern," he said in his latest annual report.

The exchange rate of the rand was "so uncertain (in 1996/97) that I do not feel able to make a meaningful forecast for earnings, other than to say that it will be difficult to repeat the performance of 1996, a year in which the value of the rand declined by 20 percent."

In addition, the downward pressure on freight rates had had a significant effect on the world's international shipping companies, which were the customers of container division, Textainer, Jowell said.
The shipping lines were responding by forming alliances, sharing equipment (including containers), negotiating lower container lease rates and generally reducing costs.

"To prosper in the more difficult and competitive environment, Textainer has taken action to enhance customer service, strengthen electronic data interchange capabilities, reduce costs and improve the monitoring and control of interest rate and credit risk," Jowell said.
One positive development for Textainer had been that containers were costing much less than they did last year. But this was not good news for Trencor's container manufacturing division.
"In the Far East the usually competitive situation is exacerbated by severe price cutting while worldwide there is a cyclical decline in demand," Jowell said.
Trencor had also been affected by the "summary reduction" in the general export incentive (GEIS).

The fact that government had cut GEIS benefits ahead of the original schedule had created severe problems because Trencor was committed to long-term contracts in which the costs have now been significantly increased.
